parts.title: Binary numbers (e)
parts.text:
In a computer system, real numbers are stored using floating-point representation with:

- 8 bits for the mantissa
- 4 bits for the exponent
- two's complement form for both the mantissa and the exponent

Calculate the normalised floating-point representation of -10.75 in this system. Show your working.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Represent as fixed-point: 01010.11 (1)
Normalise as floating-point: 01010.11 = 0.101011 × 2⁴ (1)
Represent exponent in binary: 4₁₀ = 0100₂
Apply two's complement on normalised mantissa: flip 0.101011 → 1.010100, add 1 → 1.010101 (1)
Mantissa – 10101010, Exponent – 0100 (1)

Alternative solution:
Apply two's complement on fixed-point: flip 01010.11 → 10101.00, add 1 → 10101.01 (1)
Normalise as floating-point: 10101.01 = 1.010101 × 2⁴ (1)
Represent exponent in binary: 4₁₀ = 0100₂
[Max: 4]
scheme.model_answer:
Working: 10.75 = 01010.11 = 0.101011 × 2⁴; two's complement → 1.010101
Mantissa: 10101010
Exponent: 0100

parts.title: Operating systems and user interfaces (a)(i)
parts.text:
Identify the most suitable type of operating system based on the description.

Description: A medical device, such as a heart rate monitor, uses this type of OS to ensure the system responds to critical inputs, such as heart signals, immediately.

Type of OS:

scheme.mark_scheme: Real-Time / RTOS (1)
scheme.model_answer: Real-time operating system

parts.title: Operating systems and user interfaces (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Description: In a large company, this type of OS is used to process payroll at the end of each month. The data is collected, processed, and executed without user interaction.

Type of OS:

scheme.mark_scheme: Batch processing / Batch (1)
scheme.model_answer: Batch processing operating system

parts.title: Operating systems and user interfaces (b)(i)
parts.text:
For human interaction with an operating system, a user interface is necessary.

Describe **two** advantages of using a command line interface (CLI) instead of a graphical user interface (GUI).

scheme.mark_scheme:
CLI consumes less system resources (CPU, memory) (1)
CLI is well-suited for remote administration (1)
CLI requires less bandwidth (1)
CLI allows advanced users / users with experience to execute tasks faster by typing commands directly (1)
[Max: 2] Allow other right answers.
scheme.model_answer:
1 A CLI uses fewer system resources such as CPU time and memory.
2 Experienced users can carry out tasks faster by typing commands directly.
scheme.ai_instructions: Allow other correct advantages of CLI over GUI.

parts.title: Operating systems and user interfaces (b)(ii)
parts.text:
A natural language interface is shown in the picture.

questions.title: Computer architecture
questions.text: Modern computer systems use the architecture proposed by John von Neumann.

parts.title: Computer architecture (a)
parts.text:
Name the components A, B, and C in the diagram.

![Von Neumann diagram: boxes CPU, A, Video controller and Keyboard controller connected by three buses labelled B (dotted), C (dashed) and Control bus (solid). Arrows on bus B go both ways; arrows on bus C point from the CPU towards the other components.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2026-p1/q3-buses.png)

scheme.mark_scheme:
A – Main memory / Memory / RAM (1)
B – Data bus, C – Address bus (1)
[2]

points.criterion: B – data bus and C – address bus

scheme.model_answer:
A: Main memory (RAM)
B: Data bus
C: Address bus

parts.title: Computer architecture (b)
parts.text: Describe **one** function of the CPU.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Managing data flow within the computer system / fetch-execute cycle (1)
Executing instructions from programs (1)
Performing all calculations / arithmetical and logical operations (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: The CPU fetches and executes the instructions of programs.

parts.title: Computer architecture (c)(i)
parts.text:
The main types of processors in computer systems are RISC and CISC.

Describe **two** reasons why RISC instructions are executed faster than CISC instructions.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Each RISC instruction is completed in one cycle (1)
RISC instructions are of fixed length (1)
Pipeline can be implemented (1)
Instructions are moved from register to register (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer:
1 Each RISC instruction is completed in one clock cycle.
2 RISC instructions have a fixed length, so pipelining can be used.

parts.title: Computer architecture (c)(ii)
parts.text: Describe **one** reason why CISC consumes more power than RISC.

scheme.mark_scheme:
CISC processes complex operations (1)
CISC processes instructions over multiple clock cycles (1)
CISC processor requires more transistors (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: A CISC processor needs more transistors to carry out its complex instructions.

parts.title: Computer architecture (d)
parts.text:
The fetch-execute cycle consists of three main stages: fetch, decode, and execute.

Describe the *decode* stage.

scheme.mark_scheme:
The CPU interprets the fetched instruction to determine what action is required / identify command of processor (1)
Identify addressing mode (1)
The control unit decodes the instruction format, identifying the operation/opcode and the operand (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer: The control unit interprets the fetched instruction to work out what action is required, splitting it into the opcode and the operand.

parts.title: Computer architecture (e)(i)
parts.text:
The registers involved in the fetch-execute cycle are shown in the diagram.

![Diagram of the fetch-execute cycle: PC → ? → RAM → MDR → CIR (Fetch), → CU (Decode), → ALU (Execute) → ACC.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2026-p1/q3-registers.png)

Name the missing register and describe its purpose.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Name: MAR / Memory address register (1)
Purpose: The MAR contains the address of the current instruction to be carried out (1)
[2]
scheme.model_answer:
Name: MAR (Memory Address Register)
Purpose: holds the address of the memory location of the current instruction (data) to be fetched.

parts.title: Computer architecture (e)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the purpose of ACC (Accumulator) register.

scheme.mark_scheme: The accumulator is used to store intermediate/temporary results of arithmetic or logical operations. [1]
scheme.model_answer: The ACC stores the intermediate (temporary) results of arithmetic and logical operations.

parts.title: Computer architecture (f)(i)
parts.text:
Improving your computer's performance depends on several key factors.

scheme.mark_scheme: Bus width is the number of data bits the bus can transfer in one clock cycle. [1]

questions.title: Main memory
questions.text: Main memory is the primary storage where the operating system, application programs, and data currently being processed are stored for quick access by the CPU.

parts.title: Main memory (a)
parts.text: Define the term *volatile memory*.

scheme.mark_scheme: Computer memory that loses its contents when the power is turned off. [1]
scheme.model_answer: Memory that loses its contents when the power is turned off.

parts.title: Main memory (b)
parts.text:
Suggest **one** way to prevent the error in the image below from occurring during an operation.

![Error message box: Not enough memory to complete this operation, with an OK button.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2026-p1/q4-error.png)

scheme.mark_scheme:
Increase RAM (1)
Increase virtual memory / page file (1)
Reduce application cache sizes (1)
Close some programs/applications (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: Install more RAM.

parts.title: Main memory (c)
parts.text: Explain **one** problem that may arise when using virtual memory.

scheme.mark_scheme:
System slowdown (1) because the system spends too much time moving data between RAM and disk (1)
OR
Decrease of data processing speed (1) Reading from virtual memory / secondary storage slower than RAM / main memory (1)
OR
Increased wear on the hard drive or SSD (1) because disk reads and writes occur more frequently (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer: The computer slows down, because a lot of time is spent moving data between RAM and the disk, which is much slower than RAM.

parts.title: Main memory (d)
parts.text: Explain why access to data in cache memory is faster than access to data in RAM.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Cache memory is physically located closer/in the CPU than RAM (1), which reduces the time it takes to access data (1)
OR
Cache is much smaller than RAM (1), allowing the CPU to search and retrieve data faster (1)
OR
Cache uses SRAM (1). SRAM retains data without needing constant refresh / SRAM has lower latency (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer: Cache is located in or very close to the CPU, so the data has a much shorter distance to travel and is accessed in less time.

questions.title: Backup and disk mirroring
questions.text: Information protection methods such as backup and disk mirroring can prevent data loss in case of physical device failures.

parts.title: Backup and disk mirroring (a)
parts.text: Describe how backup helps prevent data loss in the event of a fire.

scheme.mark_scheme:
If the original data is destroyed in a fire, the backup can be used to restore it (1)
Copy on the cloud automatically stores data on remote servers not affected by a fire (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: If the original data is destroyed in the fire, it can be restored from the backup copy.

parts.title: Backup and disk mirroring (b)
parts.text: Suggest **one** recommendation to ensure that the latest data is not lost in the event of a fire.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Perform backups after every critical change (1)
A copy of the documents/files should be stored in a location separate from the fire area (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: Store the backup copies in a different building / off site, away from the fire area.

parts.title: Backup and disk mirroring (c)
parts.text: Describe **one** advantage of disk mirroring over backup.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Instant data recovery in case of one disk failure (1)
Work of the system without interruption (1)
Provides business continuity as real-time data is synchronised on the second disk (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: If one disk fails, the system keeps working without interruption using the mirrored disk.

questions.title: Cloud technologies and privacy
questions.text: A company is considering moving its customers' data to the cloud. However, employees have raised concerns about security, ethical risks, and privacy policies.

parts.title: Cloud technologies and privacy (a)
parts.text: Describe **two** advantages of using cloud technologies for the company.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Reduces the need to purchase, upgrade, and maintain expensive hardware and servers (description of cost savings) (1)
Allows to easily and quickly increase or decrease the amount of data stored (description of scalability) (1)
Employees can access corporate data from anywhere in the world (description of availability) (1)
Backup minimizes the risk of data loss in the event of hardware failures or other disasters (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer:
1 The company does not need to buy and maintain expensive servers.
2 Employees can access the data from anywhere in the world.

parts.title: Cloud technologies and privacy (b)
parts.text: Provide **two** examples of risks when storing customer data using cloud technologies.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Vulnerability of data in transit (1)
Hacking and unauthorized access (1)
Unreliability of the cloud service provider (1)
Incorrect access rights settings (1)
Dependence on third parties (1)
Malware attacks (1)
[Max: 2] Accept other correct answers.
scheme.model_answer:
1 Hacking and unauthorised access
2 Dependence on the cloud provider (third party)

parts.title: Cloud technologies and privacy (c)
parts.text: Describe **two** measures that can be taken to support and enforce a privacy policy.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Ensure data is encrypted in transit and stored in the cloud (1)
Implement multi-factor authentication (1)
Clear access rights for limited access to sensitive data (1)
Conduct periodic vulnerability audits and security compliance (1)
Be open with customers about what data is collected and how it is protected (1)
Give customers control over their data / Access to data with permission (1)
[Max: 2] Accept other correct answers.
scheme.model_answer:
1 Encrypt the customer data both in transit and when stored in the cloud.
2 Set clear access rights so only authorised staff can see sensitive data.

questions.title: Programming languages and translators
questions.text: There are different types of programming languages.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (a)(i)
parts.text: Describe **one** reason why it is easier to develop a program in a high-level language than in a low-level language.

scheme.mark_scheme:
High-level languages are closer to natural language (1)
High-level languages use human-understandable constructs (1)
High-level languages use ready-made solutions (1)
High-level languages do not require knowledge of computer architecture (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: High-level languages are closer to natural language, so the code is easier to write and understand.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe **one** reason why programs in low-level languages are executed faster than in high-level languages.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Low-level languages do not require extra time for translation and processing by hardware (1)
Low-level languages provide complete control over system resources (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: Low-level programs need no extra translation time and give the programmer complete control of the hardware.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (b)(i)
parts.text:
High-level languages use translators such as compilers and interpreters.

Explain why a compiled program runs faster in comparison with an interpreted program.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Compiler translates the entire program into machine code at once (1) while an interpreter translates the code line by line during execution (1)
OR
Compiler produces an independent executable file that does not require retranslation (1) while an interpreter must translate each line of code at run time (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer: A compiler translates the whole program into machine code before it runs, whereas an interpreter has to translate each line while the program is running.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe **one** reason why an interpreter uses less memory during translation than a compiler.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Interpreter only stores the statement currently being executed (1)
Compiler stores the entire program as an executable file (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: An interpreter only keeps the statement currently being executed in memory.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (c)(i)
parts.text:
The source code is translated into an object file during the compilation stages.

Name the compilation stage at which the data stream is split into tokens.

scheme.mark_scheme: Lexical analysis [1]
scheme.model_answer: Lexical analysis

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (c)(ii)
parts.text: State **two** results of the optimisation of the source code.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Execution speed is increased (1)
Main memory usage is decreased (1)
[2]
scheme.model_answer:
1 The program runs faster.
2 The program uses less main memory.

parts.title: Programming languages and translators (c)(iii)
parts.text: Describe the purpose of syntactic analysis.

scheme.mark_scheme: To check if the sequence of tokens follows the grammatical rules of the programming language [1]
scheme.model_answer: It checks that the sequence of tokens follows the grammar (syntax) rules of the programming language.

questions.title: URLs and secure web pages
questions.text:
Aidar opened a webpage in a web browser to log into the employer's website. The webpage is shown in the picture below.

![Browser window with the address http://work.company.com/login/signin.php showing a Log in form with Username and Password fields, a Log in button, Remember me, Forgot Password? and Create an Account.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2026-p1/q8-login-page.png)

parts.title: URLs and secure web pages (a)
parts.text: Identify the parts of the webpage URL.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Protocol – http
Domain name – work.company.com
Path – login/signin.php
[1]
scheme.model_answer:
Protocol: http
Domain name: work.company.com
Path: /login/signin.php

parts.title: URLs and secure web pages (b)
parts.text: Identify the second-level domain of the webpage URL.

scheme.mark_scheme: company [1]
scheme.model_answer: company
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept 'company'. 'company.com' shows the second-level domain with its TLD — accept.

parts.title: URLs and secure web pages (c)
parts.text: Describe the purpose of the generic top-level domain of the webpage URL.

scheme.mark_scheme: A top-level domain is created to designate domains for commercial businesses [1]
scheme.model_answer: The .com top-level domain shows that the website belongs to a commercial business.

parts.title: URLs and secure web pages (d)
parts.text: Explain why user data submitted on this webpage is not secure.

scheme.mark_scheme:
The webpage uses HTTP instead of HTTPS (1)
HTTP transmits data in plaintext / without HTTPS the connection lacks encryption / making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks (1)
[2]
scheme.model_answer: The page uses HTTP instead of HTTPS, so the username and password are sent as plain text without encryption and can be intercepted.

questions.title: Client-server model and IP addresses
questions.text:
The client-server model is used in networking.

![Diagram of a server in the centre connected by two-way arrows to four clients.](https://icnwfwszbwyewktnnupl.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/media/mocks/nis-2026-p1/q9-client-server.png)

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (a)
parts.text: Describe the primary role of a server in the client-server model.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Providing resources or services to clients (1)
Hosting applications or storing data that clients can use (1)
Responding to client requests (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: The server provides resources and services to the clients and responds to their requests.

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (b)
parts.text: Describe **two** disadvantages of the client-server model.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Potential server overload if too many clients request resources at the same time / DDOS attack (1)
Increased difficulty in protecting the server from attacks, since it often stores sensitive data and is easily visible (1)
A server failure results in a huge number of clients losing access to data (1)
[Max: 2]
scheme.model_answer:
1 If the server fails, all clients lose access to the data.
2 The server can be overloaded when too many clients send requests at once.

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (c)(i)
parts.text:
To access the server, clients use the server's IP address.

Define the term *IP address*.

scheme.mark_scheme:
A unique numerical identifier assigned to each device on a network (1)
An address that identifies the location of a device on a network (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: A unique numerical address that identifies a device on a network.

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Identify the class of the IP address 192.168.1.120.

Class:

scheme.model_answer: C

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the network portion and the host portion of the IP address 192.168.1.120 with the subnet mask 255.255.255.224. Show your working.

scheme.mark_scheme:
255.255.255.224 = 11111111.11111111.11111111.11100000 → 27 bits for Network, 5 bits for Host (1 mark for solution)
.120 = .01111000 → 01100000 = 96, 00011000 = 24
Network: 192.168.1.96 or the same in binary (1 mark for correct network)
Host: 24 or the same in binary (1 mark for correct host)
[3]

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (c)(iv)
parts.text: Explain how a public IP address is different in comparison with a private IP address.

scheme.mark_scheme:
A public IP address is assigned to a device that is directly connected to the Internet (1) while a private IP address is used in private networks such as LANs or intranets (1)
OR
A public IP address is accessible to all Internet users (1), while a private IP address can only be accessed within a private network (1)
[Max: 2] Accept other correct comparison of IP addresses.
scheme.model_answer: A public IP address is used by a device connected directly to the Internet and can be reached by any Internet user, while a private IP address is only used and reachable inside a private network such as a LAN.

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (d)
parts.text: Name the device that transmits data packets in the network using IP addresses.

scheme.mark_scheme: Router [1]
scheme.model_answer: Router

parts.title: Client-server model and IP addresses (e)
parts.text: Name the OSI model layer at which the IP protocol operates.

scheme.mark_scheme: Network layer [1]
scheme.model_answer: Network layer
